BM25.query: Explain Scaled Dot-Product Attention and why scaling is necessary.
BM25.answer: Scaled Dot-Product Attention computes attention weights as softmax(QK^T / sqrt(d_k))V. [1] The scaling factor 1/sqrt(d_k) counteracts large dot-product magnitudes in higher dimensions that would otherwise push the softmax into regions with extremely small gradients. [1]

BM25.query: How does Multi-Head Attention differ from single-head attention?

BM25.query: Explain the role of positional encodings in the Transformer.
BM25.answer: In the decoder, positional encodings represent token ordering while causal masking prevents future position attention, allowing autoregressive generation with accurate temporal awareness. [1]

BM25.query: Why does self-attention enable faster training than recurrent layers?

BM25.reference: Self-attention layers execute O(1) sequential operations per layer, enabling complete parallelization across all sequence positions during training, unlike recurrent layers which require O(n) sequential steps.

BM25.query: Explain the position-wise feed-forward networks in the Transformer.

BM25.reference: Each layer in the encoder and decoder contains a fully connected feed-forward network consisting of two linear transformations with a ReLU activation in between: FFN(x) = max(0, xW1 + b1)W2 + b2, applied identically and separately to each position.

BM25.query: What is masked multi-head attention in the decoder and why is it required?
